topic: Cyclone Remal damage and return to service
wiki_text: The Summit LNG FSRU terminal off Moheshkhali Island was damaged by Cyclone Remal on 26 May 2024, when a broken floating pontoon struck the FSRU and damaged its ballast water tank. The vessel (FSRU Summit LNG) was towed to the Seatrium yard in Singapore for repairs and returned to Bangladesh in July 2024, sustaining a further minor mooring/DTM-buoy line issue on arrival. By 11 September 2024 the terminal had resumed ship-to-ship transfer and regasification, sending out roughly 500 mmcfd to the national grid. As of December 2025 the terminal had completed its 250th ship-to-ship operation and supplied approximately 13% of Bangladesh's total gas demand during FY2024-25.

On 8 November 2023 Petrobangla signed a non-binding term-sheet (alongside three related agreements) with Excelerate Energy's Bangladesh outfit to build a 4.5 mtpa FSRU near Payra seaport, together with a ~60-70 km subsea regasified-LNG pipeline from a mooring facility near Kuakata to southern Khulna, under a special law that bypassed competitive tender. In October 2024 Bangladesh's interim government scrapped the term-sheet (one week after cancelling Summit's third-FSRU deal) as part of a broader rollback of LNG agreements signed under the prior government. Petrobangla issued a letter terminating the non-binding agreement; the accord was set to lapse automatically on 7 November 2024 absent extension. With the sponsoring agreement scrapped and no replacement developer named, the project's active 'proposed' status is in doubt.

The Bangladesh government cancelled the Terminal Use Agreement and Implementation Agreement with Summit LNG Terminal 2 Co Ltd (SLNG II) for the country's third FSRU (offshore Moheshkhali Island) on 7 October 2024. Petrobangla's 14 January 2025 notice stated the termination was based on the performance bond being submitted by Summit's local parent (SCL) rather than SLNG II, non-compliance with the agreed template, and submission outside the 90-day deadline. Summit disputes the termination as invalid, says it had already invested ~US$20 million, and appealed; the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court stayed the government's re-tender process pending resolution of the legal dispute. The terminal remains cancelled in GEM pending the outcome.

topic: Tokyo Gas feasibility study for land-based Matarbari terminal
wiki_text: Tokyo Gas Co Ltd completed a full feasibility study for Bangladesh's first land-based LNG-import terminal at Matarbari Island (7.5 mtpa), covering detailed technical assessments and preparation of bid packages and requests for proposals (RfPs). The terminal is envisaged under a Build-Own-Operate-Transfer (BOOT) model with a 20-year operating period before transfer to the government. As of the study's completion, Petrobangla had not yet issued an open tender or initiated government-to-government talks, and the project remained delayed by land-acquisition issues, including a pending Tk 30 billion purchase of 'ash land' from Coal Power Generation Company Bangladesh Ltd (CPGCBL).
